title: Integration by substitution & by parts
examples: When should I use substitution instead of parts?
What is the main difference between the two methods?
Can I use both methods on the same integral?

explain.say: Today we look at two ways to integrate. These are substitution and parts. Both help us solve tricky integrals.
First we learn u-substitution. This is like reversing the chain rule for differentiation. You choose a part of the function to be your u.

If you let u equal a function, you must also find the differential du. Then you rewrite everything in terms of u and du. For example, to integrate x squared times e to the x, we choose u equals x. Then du is one. This is not a good choice for this problem.
Next we look at integration by parts. This method uses a formula to transform an integral. The formula is u times dv equals s minus integral of s d v. We choose u and dv based on the LIATE rule.

items: Choose u and dv using LIATE

explain.say: For the integral x e to the x, we choose u equals x. Then we choose dv equals e to the x dx. This makes du equal to one dx. And v equals e to the x. Now we use the formula. The result is x e to the x minus the integral of e to the x dx. This gives x e to the x minus e to the x.

items: Apply formula: x e^x - ∫ e^x dx

draw.text: ∫ x e^x dx = x e^x - e^x

faq.q: When should I use integration by substitution?
faq.a: Use substitution when you see a function and its derivative inside the integral. If one part is the derivative of another part, substitution is usually best. You might also ask if I should use substitution first.
asks: Should I use u-sub or parts?
When is substitution better than parts?

faq.q: What does the LIATE rule help me with?
faq.a: LIATE helps you decide which part of the integrand should be u. It stands for Logarithmic, Inverse trigonometric, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential. You choose u based on this order.
asks: How do I pick u for integration by parts?

faq.q: What is the formula for integration by parts?
faq.a: The formula is the integral of u times dv equals u times v minus the integral of v times du. Remember to always keep track of u, dv, du, and v.
asks: Can you write out the integration by parts formula?

faq.q: What do I do with limits when I use substitution?
faq.a: When using substitution, it is often easier to change the limits of integration. You replace the original limits with the corresponding values of u. This avoids substituting back at the end.
asks: Do I change the limits for u-sub?
How do limits change with substitution?

faq.q: Can I use both methods on the same problem?
faq.a: Sometimes you might use substitution first to simplify the integral. Then, the resulting simpler integral might require integration by parts. You solve it step by step.
asks: Is there an order to solve these?

facts: Integration by substitution reverses the chain rule.
Integration by parts uses the formula: integral of u dv equals uv minus integral of v du.
The LIATE rule helps select u when using integration by parts.
When using substitution, changing the limits of integration can simplify the process.

quiz.say: Evaluate the integral of 2x e to the x dx using integration by parts.
quiz.why: We choose u equals 2x, so du equals 2 dx. We choose dv equals e to the x dx, so v equals e to the x. Applying the formula gives 2x e to the x minus the integral of 2 e to the x dx, which is 2x e to the x minus 2 e to the x.

wrong.0: This is a common mistake from incorrectly applying the subtraction step in the formula.
wrong.1: This mistake happens if you forget that the exponential function e to the x is not just a constant.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because you forgot to multiply the constant 2 when integrating the remaining part.

quiz.say: What is the best choice for u in the integral integral of cos(x) e^x dx?
quiz.why: According to the LIATE rule, Trigonometric functions like cos(x) should be chosen as u before Exponential functions like e to the x.

wrong.1: This choice violates the LIATE rule because Trigonometric functions should come before Exponential functions.
wrong.2: You cannot choose the entire integrand as u because you must still have a remaining part to define dv.
wrong.3: Choosing u equals one simplifies nothing and does not help in applying the integration by parts formula effectively.

quiz.say: If we use substitution on integral of x e^x dx, what should u be?
quiz.why: Although this integral is better suited for parts, if we force a substitution, setting u equals x makes du equal to one dx, which is a valid, though inefficient, first step.

wrong.0: This choice makes the differentiation of u too complex to manage easily with the remaining parts.
wrong.2: Choosing u equals e to the x means du equals e to the x dx. This leaves x dx for dv, which is not easily integrable.
wrong.3: Choosing the entire integrand as u means dv would be one, which defeats the purpose of the method.
